finding.claim: Mass assignment on PUT /me. The handler copies the whole request body onto the authenticated user object and saves it. Any authenticated user can overwrite privileged or server-controlled fields on their own record, such as role, isAdmin, id, email or verified, and so escalate privileges or tamper with account state. The sibling route PUT /me/profile shows the intended allowlist of displayName and bio, and this route bypasses it.
finding.source: JSON body of an authenticated PUT /me request (req.body), fully attacker-controlled keys and values
finding.sink: req.store.save(req.user) persists the mutated user record (users.js:6). The response also echoes it back (users.js:7).

trace.note: PUT /me handler; req.user is assumed to be set by upstream auth middleware
Object.assign(req.user, req.body) merges arbitrary attacker keys into the user object with no allowlist or schema validation
req.store.save(req.user) persists the attacker-modified fields, including any role or permission fields
res.json(req.user) returns the full user object

finding.guards_checked: Searched users.js and the rest of the directory for a field allowlist, schema validation, or a field-level authorization check, and found none. Only users.js exists in the project, so upstream middleware could not be inspected. Authentication is presumably handled upstream because req.user is used. That only proves the caller is logged in and does nothing to restrict which fields they can write. The /me/profile route (users.js:11) destructures only displayName and bio, which confirms the allowlist is missing here. The exact privileged field names are unknown without the user schema. A body containing __proto__ would only change the prototype of this one user object. It would not pollute Object.prototype globally.

verdict.reason: users.js:5 runs Object.assign(req.user, req.body) with no allowlist or validation, and users.js:6 saves the result, while the sibling route at users.js:11-12 restricts input to displayName and bio. Any authenticated user can therefore write arbitrary fields on their own record. Upstream auth middleware and the user schema are not in the project, so which privileged fields exist is unknown.
